back2basics.text: Technology Readiness Level (TRL) is a scale from 1 to 9 that measures the maturity of a technology, from basic principles observed (TRL-1) to actual system proven in operational environment (TRL-9). Advancing technologies to TRL-9 means they are fully developed, tested, and ready for deployment.

2026-11-12-pm-11c6aacce7.deck: The Technology Development Board (TDB) under the Department of Science & Technology (DST) signed an agreement with Astrome Technologies for ₹64.05 crore to develop an indigenous AI-enabled Electronic Intelligence (ELINT) satellite constellation. This project aims to advance critical space and AI technologies for national security, relevant for UPSC aspirants studying science and technology in defence.

mcq.stem:
Consider the following statements about the TDB-DST agreement with Astrome Technologies:

body.label: Financial support
body.text: TDB under DST provided ₹64.05 crore through the Research, Development and Innovation Fund to Astrome Technologies for this project.

body.label: Project goal
body.text: The project aims to develop an indigenous space-based AI-enabled Electronic Intelligence (ELINT) constellation for national security applications.

body.label: Total cost and funding
body.text: The total project cost is ₹128.11 crore, with TDB funding half via Optionally Convertible Debt.

sections.heading: What is the TDB-DST agreement with Astrome about?

body.label: Key components
body.text: The project integrates three technologies: ELINT payloads, AI-based ground processing software, and inter-satellite communication links.

body.label: Satellite design
body.text: It involves developing 50 kg class microsatellites operating in low Earth orbit as part of a constellation architecture.

body.label: Technology advancement
body.text: The programme aims to advance technologies from Technology Readiness Level (TRL)-4 to TRL-9 through development, integration, testing, and validation.

sections.heading: What technologies and capabilities does the project involve?

body.label: Strategic importance
body.text: Space-based systems provide persistent surveillance over large areas, crucial for intelligence gathering and national security.

body.label: Indigenous capability
body.text: Developing indigenous ELINT and AI technologies reduces dependence on foreign systems and strengthens strategic autonomy.

body.label: Technology convergence
body.text: The project combines satellite engineering, electronic intelligence, artificial intelligence, and secure space communications.

back2basics.text: The judiciary can direct government bodies and institutions to uphold rights and protections for vulnerable groups, such as LGBTQIA+ students, especially when their safety and mental health are at risk. Courts may enforce guidelines or laws to prevent discrimination, bullying, and harassment in schools to ensure an inclusive and safe learning environment.

2026-11-12-pm-1f332d1306.deck: The Punjab and Haryana High Court directed Haryana education authorities and CBSE to implement Supreme Court guidelines on student mental health and suicide prevention following a petition about bullying and assault of an LGBTQIA+ student. This ruling highlights judicial intervention in safeguarding vulnerable students' rights in educational institutions.

back2basics.text: Climate finance refers to funds provided by developed countries to developing countries to help them mitigate and adapt to the impacts of climate change. It supports projects like renewable energy, disaster resilience, and sustainable infrastructure. These funds can come as grants, loans, or investments and are a crucial part of international climate agreements.

2026-11-12-pm-70459f40b2.deck: At the 2026 UN Climate Summit in Türkiye, disagreements over climate finance resurfaced, highlighting the gap between funds pledged by wealthy nations and the actual support received by developing countries. Understanding this dispute is crucial for grasping global climate governance and India's position in international climate negotiations.

editor.why: Climate finance is critical for global climate action and India’s commitments under international frameworks.

mains.demand: Explain the recurring issues in climate finance at UN summits and analyze their impact on India's climate goals and international climate diplomacy.
mains.question: Discuss the challenges of climate finance in global climate negotiations and their implications for India.

body: Outline the recurring disputes over the adequacy, accessibility, and terms of climate finance between developed and developing countries.

structure.conclusion: Addressing climate finance challenges is essential for equitable and effective global climate action and for India to meet its climate objectives.
structure.intro: Climate finance remains a contentious issue in global climate negotiations, affecting the implementation of climate actions in developing countries.

mcq.stem:
Consider the following statements about climate finance at UN climate summits:
1. Developing countries primarily dispute the total amount of climate finance pledged by wealthy nations.
2. Developing countries focus on how much climate finance actually reaches them and the terms of that finance.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
mcq.trap: Statement 1 is a common misconception; the dispute is not mainly about the total pledged but about the actual disbursement and terms of climate finance, as emphasized by developing countries.

body.label: Divergent perspectives
body.text: Wealthy countries highlight the increasing amounts of climate finance they mobilize, while developing countries question how much of this money actually reaches them and under what conditions.

body.label: Developmental needs
body.text: For countries like India and others in the Global South, climate finance is essential not just for accounting but for practical needs such as protecting agriculture from drought, urban areas from floods, and populations from extreme heat.

body.label: Use of funds
body.text: Developing countries emphasize that climate finance should support expanding energy access, infrastructure, and job creation through cleaner power to meet the costs of a warming world.

sections.heading: What causes recurring disputes over climate finance at UN summits?

body.label: Enabling adaptation and mitigation
body.text: Climate finance helps make ambitious goals affordable by funding measures that protect vulnerable sectors and promote sustainable development.

body.label: India’s international commitments
body.text: India’s climate goals depend on adequate and timely climate finance to implement adaptation strategies and transition to cleaner energy.

body.label: Global equity and trust
body.text: Resolving climate finance disputes is key to building trust between developed and developing countries, which is essential for effective global climate governance.

back2basics.text: The PLI Scheme is a government initiative to boost domestic manufacturing by providing financial incentives linked to production output. It aims to attract investment, enhance capacity, and improve competitiveness in strategic sectors such as advanced battery manufacturing. The scheme supports India's goal of self-reliance and reducing import dependence.

2026-11-12-pm-a02061032d.deck: The Ministry of Heavy Industries received 22 bids for establishing 10 GWh Advanced Chemistry Cell (ACC) manufacturing capacity under the PLI ACC Scheme, part of a 50 GWh national target. This development highlights India's push to build a domestic ACC manufacturing ecosystem to support energy storage and renewable energy expansion.

body.label: Scheme approval and budget
body.text: In May 2021, the Union Cabinet approved the PLI Scheme for the National Programme on Advanced Chemistry Cell Battery Storage with a budgetary outlay of ₹18,100 crore to achieve 50 GWh ACC manufacturing capacity in India.

body.label: Scheme goals
body.text: The scheme aims to enhance domestic ACC manufacturing capabilities and attract large domestic and international players to build a globally competitive ACC ecosystem.

body.label: Energy security and value chain
body.text: The scheme supports India's growing energy storage needs from renewable energy expansion, contributing to energy security and deepening the domestic ACC technology value chain.

sections.heading: What is the PLI ACC Scheme and its objectives?

body.label: Bid details
body.text: The Ministry of Heavy Industries received 22 bids for 10 GWh ACC manufacturing capacity earmarked for Grid-Scale Stationary Storage applications as part of the 50 GWh target.

body.label: Tender process
body.text: The global tender was floated on 15 July 2026 on the Central Public Procurement Portal, with technical bids opened on 11 November 2026 using a transparent two-stage Quality and Cost Based Selection mechanism.

body.label: List of bidders
body.text: Bidders include prominent firms such as ACME Solar Holdings Ltd., Amara Raja Advanced Cell Technologies Pvt. Ltd., Reliance Industries Ltd., JSW Neo Energy Ltd., and others.

sections.heading: What is the recent development in ACC manufacturing bids?

body.label: Strengthening domestic manufacturing
body.text: The bids reflect strong industry interest and government commitment to building a self-reliant and globally competitive ACC manufacturing ecosystem.

body.label: Supporting renewable energy
body.text: The 10 GWh capacity for Grid-Scale Stationary Storage will support India's rapidly growing renewable energy storage requirements.

body.label: Vision alignment
body.text: This initiative aligns with the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047 to develop advanced technology manufacturing capabilities.
